security_audit.summary: The static alerts reflect manual installation, Markdown formatting, visual prompts, and a public source citation. content.user_title: Build Image Prompt Packs for Short Videos
content.value_statement: Separate image prompts can produce covers, characters, and scenes that do not match. Build a reusable prompt pack with shared visual rules and clear instructions for each asset.
actual_capabilities: Turn scripts, Obsidian video notes, or rough ideas into numbered image prompts with aspect ratios, framing, and lighting.
Draft vertical cover prompts with a clear focal subject, space for a title, and no rendered text by default.
Plan three to eight linked storyboard keyframes, including first and last frames, with shared continuity rules.
Define fixed character traits for turnaround views, expression sheets, pose sheets, and stickers.
Draft prompts for matching props, backgrounds, and isolated cutouts, with a solid background option when transparency is unavailable.
Write prompts for background changes, canvas extension, and pose or expression revisions while listing what should stay unchanged.
limitations: Produces text prompts, not rendered images, edited files, or finished videos.
Does not install Gemini, Nano Banana, or a video generation tool.
Character consistency depends on the image model and may require a reference image.
True transparency depends on the image tool and may require separate background removal.

use_cases.title: Plan a vertical video cover
use_cases.description: Turn a video idea into a 9:16 cover prompt with one focal subject and clear space for a title overlay.

use_cases.title: Storyboard a short explainer
use_cases.description: Convert a script into linked keyframe prompts with a consistent palette, setting, and lighting.

use_cases.title: Build a reusable mascot pack
use_cases.description: Define the mascot's fixed traits, then draft prompts for turnaround views, reactions, poses, and cutouts.

prompt_templates.title: Write one cover prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Start with a topic and a platform.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one 9:16 Gemini cover prompt for [topic] on [platform]. Leave the upper third clear for my title. Do not ask the model to render text.

prompt_templates.title: Turn a script into keyframes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Plan a short sequence from an existing script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [script] into five storyboard keyframe prompts at [aspect ratio]. Label the first and last frames. Give all five prompts one shared continuity rule.

prompt_templates.title: Define a recurring character pack
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Keep a mascot recognizable across views and reactions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image prompt pack for [character description]. Define fixed colors, proportions, and accessories. Write prompts for three turnaround views, six expressions, and six actions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare frames and matching overlays
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Plan assets for an image-to-video sequence and later compositing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [script] and [character reference description] to draft a first frame, a last frame, and two matching prop cutouts. Keep the palette, lighting, and proportions consistent. Include a solid background fallback and a continuity checklist.

output_examples.input: Write a vertical cover prompt for a balcony gardening tutorial.
output_examples.output: Frame one bright tomato seedling at the center of a 9:16 image in soft morning light. Leave the upper third blank for a title. Do not render text.

output_examples.input: Plan three storyboard frames for an animated robot planting a seed.
output: Continuity: Use the same blue robot, yellow gloves, clay style, and soft window light in every frame.
First frame: Show the robot holding one seed above an empty pot in a medium shot.
Middle frame: Cut to a close-up of the yellow gloves placing the seed into the soil.
Last frame: Use a wide shot as the robot slides the planted pot toward the window.

best_practices: State the target platform, aspect ratio, and asset purpose before drafting prompts.
Define the character palette, proportions, and accessories before describing new poses or expressions.
Review generated previews at phone size and compare adjacent frames before using them in a video.
anti_patterns: Asking for a finished video when the deliverable is a text prompt pack.
Changing the character design, lighting, and palette between shots that need to match.
Asking the image model to draw a title when the title will be added during editing.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images or videos?
faq.answer: No. It writes prompts and continuity notes. Run the prompts in your chosen image tool and use a separate video tool as needed.

faq.question: What can I use as input?
faq.answer: Start with a script, a video note, a character description, or a short concept. Add the target platform and visual style when known.

faq.question: How many storyboard frames does it plan?
faq.answer: The default is five keyframes. Ask for three to eight when your story needs a different number.

faq.question: Can it keep my character identical in every image?
faq.answer: No. It repeats key design traits to improve consistency. Use a reference image in your image tool when the character must match closely.

faq.question: What if my tool cannot generate a transparent background?
faq.answer: Ask for a plain white or green background and a clear outline. Remove that background later in your editing tool.

faq.question: Can I request prompts in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The default pairs Chinese explanations with concise English prompts. You can request English, Chinese, or bilingual prompts.
